newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major avoid Euro defeat in parliament.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major avoid Euro defeat in parliament.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major won two crucial votes over the European Union on Monday night, surviving the first real test of the British government's unity since it lost its overall majority in the House of Commons last week.
The Conservative government won a vote on its stance on the EU fishing policy by 316 votes to 304, just minutes after defeating a challenge from the Labour party by 316-305.
A by-election victory for the opposition Labour Party last week left the Conservatives level in terms of seats -- 323 -- in the House of Commons with the combined forces of the opposition.

Major faced a real challenge to win through. The Conservatives are deeply split over the EU and fishing is an emotional issue for MPs of the ruling party with coastal constituencies who are afraid of losing their seats at the looming election.
But the government offered concessions to fishermen in Northern Ireland to convince a group of Northern Irish Protestant MPs to abstain in the vote.

Potential Conservative rebels -- angry at foreign boats fishing in British waters -- were brought back on board with the promise that the government would take a tough line in talks on the EU's future unless the grave problems of Britain's fishing industry are dealt with.
The government soldiered on after it was defeated by just two in a similar vote on fishing a year ago.
But since then, the Conservatives' majority in parliament has been wiped out by defections and by-election losses. Any slip-up could now force Major into an early general election.

With his party more than 20 points behind Tony Blair's Labour in the latest opinion polls, Major is hoping to hang on as long as possible to reap the benefit of tax cuts due to work their way through into wage packets in April.
Major has indicated he has in mind an election on May 1, just three weeks before the last possible date.
Speculation has been growing that he may be forced to hold the vote earlier. But Monday's victory will give him a breathing space.
The House of Commons is due to to break up for the Christmas holidays next week, giving Major a respite from the threat of a political ambush ever-present in parliament.
